explanation: Brother of Moses and the first high priest in Israel, chosen by God to serve as a priest.
Prophet and leader of the people of Israel, who led them out of Egypt and received the law from God on Mount Sinai.
The highest religious leader in Israel, responsible for performing sacrifices and other ritual acts in the tabernacle or temple.
The ceremony in which Aaron and his sons were consecrated as priests, including anointing with oil and being clothed in priestly garments.
A gift to God, usually consisting of animals or food items, that was burned on an altar as a symbolic act to honor God and seek atonement for sins.
A special mixture of olive oil and spices used to anoint priests and holy objects, symbolizing God's blessing and presence.
Special clothing worn by priests during their service, including the ephod, breastplate, robe, turban, and sash, which symbolized their role as servants of God.
A symbol of life and cleansing in the Old Testament, used in sacrifices and ceremonies to cleanse and sanctify people and objects.
